title: Information Theory & Divergences
description: Study entropy and coding intuition, cross entropy and kl divergence, mutual information, and variational bounds and elbo. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Entropy and coding intuition
lessons.description: Calculate entropy for a binary distribution with probabilities one and zero using the zero-term convention.
lessons.conceptOverview: Entropy is expected negative log probability under a distribution. With base-two logarithms it is measured in bits; a fair binary outcome has one bit of entropy, while a certain outcome has zero.
lessons.whyItMatters: Entropy measures uncertainty under the specified distribution.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Entropy is expected negative log probability under a distribution. With base-two logarithms it is measured in bits; a fair binary outcome has one bit of entropy, while a certain outcome has zero.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Entropy is expected negative log probability under a distribution. With base-two logarithms it is measured in bits; a fair binary outcome has one bit of entropy, while a certain outcome has zero.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A fair coin requires one bit on average in an idealized code, whereas a deterministic outcome carries no uncertainty.

sections.title: Practice & verification
sections.content: Calculate entropy for a binary distribution with probabilities one and zero using the zero-term convention. Write down your reasoning and check it against the concept before continuing.

keyTakeaways: Entropy measures uncertainty under the specified distribution.
commonMistakes: Every binary variable has exactly one bit of entropy.

lessons.title: Cross entropy and KL divergence
lessons.description: Explain the consequence for negative log-likelihood and why probability smoothing may be needed.
lessons.conceptOverview: Cross entropy H(P,Q) equals H(P) plus KL(P to Q) when defined. KL is nonnegative but asymmetric, and it can be infinite if Q assigns zero probability where P has positive mass.
lessons.whyItMatters: Assigning zero probability to possible events can produce infinite log loss.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Cross entropy H(P,Q) equals H(P) plus KL(P to Q) when defined. KL is nonnegative but asymmetric, and it can be infinite if Q assigns zero probability where P has positive mass.

lessons.title: Mutual information
lessons.description: Explain why observing dependence does not prove umbrellas cause wet pavement.
lessons.conceptOverview: Mutual information measures dependence as the divergence between a joint distribution and the product of its marginals. It is zero for independence, but positive dependence does not establish causation.
lessons.whyItMatters: Mutual information measures dependence rather than causal direction.

sections.title: Concept
sections.content: Mutual information measures dependence as the divergence between a joint distribution and the product of its marginals. It is zero for independence, but positive dependence does not establish causation.

sections.title: Worked example

lessons.title: Variational bounds and ELBO
lessons.description: Identify both terms that must be considered in the objective.
lessons.conceptOverview: The evidence lower bound combines expected log-likelihood with a divergence penalty between an approximate posterior and the prior. Maximizing it jointly improves fit and controls the approximation, but a bound is not the exact log evidence.
lessons.whyItMatters: The ELBO balances reconstruction fit and a KL term.
